mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% for three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced household demand, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and drives lower S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but the average return is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which depresses wage growth and consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines persistently, or the trigger fires but the average return is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure, which increases uncertainty and reduces S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed their 12-month moving averages, or the joint trigger fires but the median return is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST exceeds its 12M MA for four months, or the trigger fires but the median return is not different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above their respective 6-month averages indicates a statistical artifact of labor force reclassification during economic expansion, which historically coincides with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and UNRATE exceed their 6M MA, or the joint trigger fires but the median return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for two consecutive quarters signals economic stagnation, which reduces corporate profit growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDP growth is persistently below 1%, or the trigger fires but the median return is positive.
